items.title: Constants & Numeric Boundaries
items.codeSnippet:
Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER; // 9007199254740991 (2^53 - 1)
Number.MIN_SAFE_INTEGER; // -9007199254740991 (-(2^53 - 1))
Infinity;                // Greater than any finite number
-Infinity;               // Smaller than any finite number
Number.EPSILON;          // 2.220446049250313e-16 (smallest delta: 1.0 + EPSILON !== 1.0)
items.gotchas: ⚠️ **Don't Forget (Precision Breakdown):** In JavaScript, all numbers are IEEE 754 64-bit floats. Beyond $2^{53} - 1$, integers lose precision: `9007199254740992 + 1 === 9007199254740992` evaluates to `true`!

items.title: ASCII Conversion Signatures
items.codeSnippet:
// Char -> ASCII Code:
str.charCodeAt(index);   // Returns 16-bit UTF-16 code unit (0-65535)
str.codePointAt(index);  // Returns full Unicode code point (handles 32-bit emojis/surrogates)

// ASCII Code -> Char:
String.fromCharCode(code);      // 0-65535
String.fromCodePoint(codePoint);// 0-1114111

// Benchmark Values:
'a'.charCodeAt(0); // 97
'z'.charCodeAt(0); // 122
'A'.charCodeAt(0); // 65
'Z'.charCodeAt(0); // 90
'0'.charCodeAt(0); // 48
'9'.charCodeAt(0); // 57
items.gotchas: ⚠️ **Don't Forget:** `'a' + 1` does NOT produce `'b'`. In JavaScript, `'a' + 1` produces `"a1"`. To advance a character: `String.fromCharCode('a'.charCodeAt(0) + 1)`.

items.title: Comparator Contract
items.summary: - Return `< 0`: `a` comes before `b` (no swap). - Return `=== 0`: `a` and `b` maintain order. - Return `> 0`: `b` comes before `a` (swap).

items.summary: - V8 uses **Timsort** (hybrid Merge/Insertion sort). - Guaranteed **stable** since ECMAScript 2019. - Time: $O(n \log n)$ average/worst-case, $O(n)$ best-case. Space: $O(n)$ auxiliary buffers. Always prefer `Map` and `Set` over plain `{}` in DSA for numeric keys, explicit `.size`, and zero prototype pollution.

items.summary: V8 crashes with `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded` when recursion depth exceeds $\approx 10,000$ frames. An explicit heap array stack has no depth limit: All bitwise operations coerce operands to **32-bit signed integers** $[-2^{31}, 2^{31} - 1]$.

items.title: Core Bitwise Operations Table
items.summary: | Operation | Expression | Purpose / Notes | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **Check $k$-th bit** | `(n & (1 << k)) !== 0` | Always wrap check in parentheses (precedence trap!) | | **Set $k$-th bit** | `n = n | (1 << k)` | Forces bit at position $k$ to 1 |
